title: The Bundle of Sticks
text:
An old farmer had several sons who could not stop quarreling. They argued over the work, over the land and over every small slight, and nothing he said made any difference. He had pleaded with them and scolded them, and still the house was full of their bickering.

One day he told them to bring him a bundle of sticks, tied tightly together. He handed it to the eldest and asked him to break it. The young man strained until his face went red, but the bundle would not give. Each brother tried in turn, and each one failed.

Then the father untied the cord and gave every son a single stick. They snapped them easily, almost without effort.

"You see," he said, "as long as you stand together, no enemy can harm you. But if you are divided among yourselves, you will be broken as easily as these sticks."
lesson: Family members who stand together can weather almost anything. Divided by petty quarrels, each of them becomes easy to break.
people: An old father, his quarreling sons
